title: Purification of micronuclei from cultured cells by flow cytometry
protocol: Seed HEK293T and HeLa cells overexpressing H2B-mCherry and GFP-cGAS fluorescent proteins 24 hours before drug treatment at desired density on an appropriate container.
For control samples, seed parental cells as well as cells overexpressing only H2B-mCherry 24 hours before drug treatment at desired density on an appropriate container.
Ensure the final volume of media in each dish is 80 mL for ideal cell growth.
Dilute the Mps1 inhibitor Reversine to a final concentration of 0.5 μM.
Incubate all cultured cells with the diluted Reversine at 37°C for 24–48 hours.
Monitor cell viability and adjust seeding density if necessary to avoid major cell loss.
Collect cell samples after treatment for further analysis.
Harvest the cultured cells in 50 mL conical tubes.
Wash cells with 30 mL PBS per cell culture dish.
Add 20 mL of pre-warmed (37°C) Trypsin per cell culture dish.
Incubate the dishes at 37°C for 10 min to enhance Trypsin activity.
Verify that the cells are detached from the dish using a microscope.
Place the dish back at 37°C and incubate for 2–5 min more if necessary.
Add 10 mL of pre-warmed (37°C) fresh culture medium and collect the cells in a 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the dish with an additional 10 mL of fresh culture medium and add this volume to the conical tube.
Collect a sample of trypsinized cells for cell counting.
Centrifuge harvested cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Discard the supernatant and retain the pelleted cells in a 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the cell pellet with fresh culture medium without FBS (first wash).
Resuspend the cell pellet using 2 mL of fresh culture medium with a 1000 μL pipette tip.
Add fresh culture medium without serum to reach the washing buffer volume as indicated in Table 1.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C (second wash).
Discard the supernatant and retain the pellet in the conical tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in pre-warmed (37°C) culture medium without FBS supplemented with cytochalasin B (final concentration of 10 μg/mL).
Incubate the cells in the medium supplemented with Cytochalasin B for 30 min at 37°C.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 5 min (at 4°C).
Discard the culture medium supplemented with Cytochalasin B and keep the cell pellet on ice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ice-cold lysis buffer using a 5 mL pipette by gently pipetting up and down 5 times.
Add additional volume of lysis buffer to reach the final volume of solution.
Transfer the cell lysate into a Dounce-homogenizer.
Gently Dounce-homogenize the sample using a loose-fitting pestle (10 strokes).
Transfer the cell lysate back into the 50 mL conical tube.
Optional verification step: Homogenize the lysate.
Collect 50 μL of the lysate and mix with an equal volume of PBS 1× + 0.5 μg/mL of DAPI.
Examine the sample under a fluorescence microscope.
The primary nuclei and micronuclei should be released from other cellular compartments.
Micronuclei and primary nuclei should be separated from each other.
Mix the cell lysate with an equal volume of Sucrose 1.8 M Buffer.
Prepare the sucrose density gradient in a 50 mL conical tube.
Pipette 10 mL of the mixture [Lysate 1:1 Sucrose 1.8 M Buffer] on top of the prepared sucrose density gradient.
Centrifuge the samples in a JS-5.3 swinging bucket rotor at 944 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Collect the upper 2 mL as Fraction 1.
Discard Fraction 1.
Collect the following 5 mL as Fraction 2.
Transfer Fraction 2 containing micronuclei to a new 50 mL conical tube.
Keep the new conical tube on ice.
Optional: Collect 50 μL of each fraction and mix with an equal volume of PBS 1× + 0.5 μg/mL DAPI.
Examine the samples under a fluorescence microscope.
Discard Fraction 3.
Collect the following 38 mL as Fraction 3.
Transfer Fraction 2 to a new conical tube for micronuclei preparation.
Dilute fraction 2 1:5 with ice-cold supplemented PBS 1×.
Centrifuge the samples in a JS-5.3 swinging bucket rotor at 944 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully, leaving around 500 μL of buffer with the pellet.
Resuspend the micronuclei pellet in ice-cold supplemented PBS 1× containing 2 μg/mL DAPI using a 1000 μL pipette tip by gently pipetting up and down 5 times.
Filter the samples through a 40 μm ministrainer into FACS tubes.
Keep filtered samples on ice in the dark.
Sort the desired samples with a BD FACSAria III Cell Sorter.
Use control samples to draw gates for total, intact, and ruptured micronuclei.
Draw an additional gate for primary nuclei if desired.
Wash the system by running water between each sample for 1 minute.
Add ice-cold supplemented PBS 1× in the collection tubes before collecting the samples.
Invert the tubes as many times as necessary to coat the interior with buffer.
Invert the sample FACS tubes 5 times to homogenize the sample.
Sort the desired gates at a flow rate of 1,500–3,000 events/s in mode 4-way purity.
Put the collection tubes on ice after sorting until further processing.
Collect 300,000 micronuclei in 1.5 mL low-binding collection tubes for immunofluorescence.
Add the appropriate volume of PFA 16% to the sample tube to reach a final concentration of 2%-4%.
Invert the tubes 5 times and incubate at 20°C-25°C for 15 min.
Transfer the tubes into cytospin funnels containing up to 500 μL each.
Cytospin the samples onto microscopy slides at 1000 rpm for 10 min at 20°C-25°C.
Let the slides air-dry at 20°C-25°C for at least 15 h.
Add BSA to the samples (final concentration 0.03%).
Add NP-40 to the samples (final concentration 0.1%).
Centrifuge in a JS-5.3 swinging bucket rotor at maximum speed for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully using pipettes, avoiding disturbing the pellet.
Keep the visible pellet and resuspend it in 500 μL ice-cold supplemented PBS 1× buffer.
Transfer the resuspended pellet into a 1.5 mL low-binding tube.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully using pipettes, avoiding disturbing the pellet.
Keep the visible pellet.
If the pellet is not visible, do not discard the supernatant and add BSA again.
Centrifuge the sample once more for 20 minutes (troubleshooting available).
Store the pellets at -80°C until performing the functional assay.
Thaw micronuclei samples on ice.
Lysate samples in 1× Laemmli buffer at a concentration of 2.5 × 10^6 micronuclei/μL.
Denature the lysates at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Sonicate the samples using a Bioruptor 300 on high intensity setting for 8 cycles (30 seconds ON, 30 seconds OFF).
If sonication is not available, shear the DNA using a 1 mL syringe until the lysate is no longer viscous.
Load lysate from 0.5 × 10^6 micronuclei in each lane of a polyacrylamide gel.
Resolve proteins by SDS-PAGE and transfer to nitrocellulose membranes.
Block membranes in Odyssey blocking buffer in TBS for Li-COR immunoblotting.
Dilute primary antibodies in blocking buffer with 0.2% Tween and incubate with membranes at least 15 hours at 4°C.
Wash membranes in TBS supplemented with 0.5% Tween three times, five minutes each.
Use secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 680 and 800) at 1:10,000 dilutions in blocking buffer with 0.2% Tween for one hour at 20°C-25°C.
Wash membranes in TBS supplemented with 0.5% Tween three times, five minutes each.
Wash membranes once in TBS without Tween for five minutes.
Dry the membranes before imaging.
Measure fluorescence using an infrared imaging scanner according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Perform non-quantitative immunoblotting as an alternative method.
Block membranes in TBS-T and milk 5% solution.
Dilute primary antibodies in TBS-T.
Dilute horseradish-peroxidase-conjugated secondary antibodies in TBS-T.
Image membranes using enhanced chemiluminescence.
